full_judgment: 144. Before parting with this case, I must remind myself that although the powers of this Division are very wide, this Court, in several judicial pronouncements, has prescribed the limits of its own power in criminal appeals. Except under exceptional circumstances it does not interfere with the findings of fact reached by the High Court Division unless this Court is of the opinion that the High Court Division had misread and misappreciated the evidence on record committing a substantial and grave miscarriage of justice. This Division normally does not reappraise the evidence if the High Court Division has approached the case before it in accordance with the guidelines laid down by this Court unless some basic error on the part of the High Court Division is brought to the notice of this Court. As a matter of fact, the High Court Division is the final Court of appeal and ours is a Court of special jurisdiction.
